paper_details.examType: Sample Question Paper for Practice Only (High School Examination - 2027)
instructions: Question Nos. 1 to 5 are 30 objective-type questions. Each question carries 1 (one) mark.
Internal options are given in question nos. 18 to 23.
Marks of each question are indicated against it.
Answer question nos. 6 to 17 in about 30 words each.
Answer question nos. 18 to 20 in about 75 words each.
Answer question nos. 21 to 23 in about 120 words each.
Draw a neat and clean labelled diagram wherever required.

questions.text: Choose the correct option:

parts.statement: Reaction of calcium oxide with water is –
parts.explanation:
Correct option is (a).

Simple Reason:
When water is added to quicklime (calcium oxide), the container becomes very hot because a large amount of heat is released. Any reaction that releases heat is called an 'Exothermic reaction'.

parts.statement: Which of the following acid-base indicators is suitable for a visually impaired student?
parts.explanation:
Correct option is (c).

Simple Reason:
Visually impaired students cannot see colour changes, so they identify acids and bases by smell. Vanilla essence is an 'olfactory indicator'—its sweet smell disappears when mixed with a base, while the smell remains in an acid.

parts.statement: A liquid non-metal is –
parts.explanation:
Correct option is (b).

Simple Reason:
Most non-metals are solids or gases, but 'Bromine' is the only non-metal that exists in a liquid state at room temperature. (Tip: Liquid metal is 'Mercury', and liquid non-metal is 'Bromine').

parts.statement: A pure tall plant (TT) is crossed with a dwarf pea plant (tt). What will be the ratio of pure tall plants to dwarf plants in the F₂ generation?
parts.explanation:
Correct option is (c).

Simple Reason:
In the F₂ generation, 4 plants are produced: 1 pure tall (TT), 2 hybrid tall (Tt), and 1 pure dwarf (tt). The question asks specifically for the ratio of 'pure tall (TT)' to 'dwarf (tt)', which is 1 : 1. (If it asked for all tall vs. dwarf plants, the ratio would be 3:1).

parts.statement: In what order is a domestic electrical circuit always connected?
parts.explanation:
Correct option is (b).

Simple Reason:
Household appliances like fans, TVs, and bulbs are connected in 'parallel' so that every appliance gets the full 220V voltage and turning off or damaging one appliance does not stop the others from working.

parts.statement: The main cause of Ozone layer depletion is –
parts.explanation:
Correct option is (a).

Simple Reason:
CFC (Chlorofluorocarbon) gas released from refrigerators and air conditioners rises to the upper atmosphere and breaks down the ozone layer, causing ozone depletion.

questions.explanation: All multiple-choice questions are based on core concepts of Class 10 Science.

questions.text: Fill in the blanks:

parts.statement: Metal oxides are generally {BLANK} in nature.
parts.explanation:
Answer: basic

Simple Reason: Metal oxides dissolve in water to form bases and turn red litmus paper blue, so they are basic in nature.

parts.statement: Brittleness is usually a major property of {BLANK}.
parts.explanation:
Answer: non-metals

Simple Reason: When hammered, non-metals (like coal or sulphur) do not flatten into sheets; instead, they break easily into pieces. This property is called brittleness.

parts.statement: μ = sin i / sin r is known as the law of {BLANK}.
parts.explanation:
Answer: Snell

Simple Reason: According to the second law of refraction, the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (sin i) to the sine of the angle of refraction (sin r) is a constant, known as Snell's law.

parts.statement: Pure water is a {BLANK} of electricity.
parts.explanation:
Answer: bad conductor (insulator)

Simple Reason: Pure (distilled) water contains no dissolved salts or free ions, so electric current cannot pass through it.

parts.statement: At the time of short circuit, the value of electric current in the circuit {BLANK}.
parts.explanation:
Answer: increases heavily

Simple Reason: During a short circuit, live and neutral wires come into direct contact, making resistance almost zero and causing the current to shoot up dangerously high.

parts.statement: An electric current always produces a {BLANK} field.
parts.explanation:
Answer: magnetic

Simple Reason: Whenever electric current flows through a wire, it behaves like a magnet and creates a magnetic field around itself.

questions.text: Write True or False:

parts.statement: A base turns red litmus blue.
parts.explanation:
Answer: True

Simple Reason: Easy memory trick: 'B-R-B' (Base turns Red to Blue). Bases always turn red litmus paper blue.

parts.statement: Metals generally form cations by losing electrons.
parts.explanation:
Answer: True

Simple Reason: Metals have 1, 2, or 3 electrons in their outermost shell, which they easily donate (lose) to form positively charged ions called cations (e.g., Na⁺, Mg²⁺).

parts.statement: Saturated hydrocarbons have only single bonds between carbon atoms.
parts.explanation:
Answer: True

Simple Reason: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes, such as methane and ethane) contain only single covalent bonds between carbon atoms.

parts.statement: In humans, the digestion of food takes place only in the stomach.
parts.explanation:
Answer: False

Simple Reason: Digestion begins in the mouth (with saliva) and is completed in the small intestine, not just in the stomach.

parts.statement: Reflex actions are always controlled by the brain.
parts.explanation:
Answer: False

Simple Reason: Sudden reflex actions (like pulling your hand back from a hot pan) are controlled immediately by the 'spinal cord', not the brain.

parts.statement: Nerve cells are called neurons.
parts.explanation:
Answer: True

Simple Reason: The structural and functional unit of the nervous system is the nerve cell, which is called a 'neuron'.

questions.text: Answer in one word / sentence:

parts.statement: Write the name of the functional group of ethanol.
parts.explanation:
Answer: Alcohol (Hydroxyl) group (–OH)

Simple Explanation: Organic compounds ending with '-ol' (like ethanol) contain the –OH functional group.

parts.statement: Name the pigment necessary for photosynthesis in plants.
parts.explanation:
Answer: Chlorophyll

Simple Explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in leaves that traps sunlight so plants can make their food.

parts.statement: Write the name of the organ that provides nutrition to the embryo from the mother.
parts.explanation:
Answer: Placenta

Simple Explanation: The placenta is a special disc-like tissue that transfers glucose and oxygen from the mother's blood to the growing baby.

parts.statement: Write the full name of genetic material.
parts.explanation:
Answer: Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA)

Simple Explanation: DNA carries hereditary traits and information from parents to their children.

parts.statement: What is the bending of light from one medium to another medium called?
parts.explanation:
Answer: Refraction of light

Simple Explanation: When light travels from air into water or glass, its speed changes, causing it to bend from its original path.

parts.statement: Write the name of the discoverer of the magnetic effect of electric current.
parts.explanation:
Answer: Hans Christian Oersted

Simple Explanation: In 1820, Oersted discovered that a compass needle deflects when placed near a wire carrying electric current.

questions.text: What happens when water is added to calcium oxide? Write the chemical equation.

parts.statement: What happens when water is added to calcium oxide? Write the chemical equation.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
When water is added to calcium oxide (quicklime), it reacts vigorously with water to form 'calcium hydroxide' (slaked lime) and releases a large amount of heat. This is both a combination and an exothermic reaction.

Chemical Equation:
CaO(s) + H₂O(l) ⟶ Ca(OH)₂(aq) + Heat

questions.text: Write the names of two natural indicators and two synthetic indicators used to identify acids and bases.

parts.statement: Write the names of two natural indicators and two synthetic indicators used to identify acids and bases.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
1. Two Natural Indicators (obtained from nature):
   • Litmus (obtained from lichen)
   • Turmeric (or red cabbage juice)

2. Two Synthetic Indicators (man-made in laboratories):
   • Methyl Orange
   • Phenolphthalein

questions.text: A student dips blue litmus paper into lemon juice. What colour change will occur and why? Give the reason.

parts.statement: A student dips blue litmus paper into lemon juice. What colour change will occur and why? Give the reason.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Colour Change: The blue litmus paper will turn 'red'.

Reason: Lemon juice contains 'citric acid'. A key property of acids is that they turn blue litmus paper red. (Memory trick: 'A-B-R' = Acid turns Blue to Red).

questions.text: Write the reason why metals like gold and silver are used to make jewellery, whereas copper and iron are not. Give the reason.

parts.statement: Write the reason why metals like gold and silver are used to make jewellery, whereas copper and iron are not. Give the reason.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Gold and silver are very low-reactive metals. They do not react with air, moisture, or mild acids, so they do not corrode and keep their shine for a long time. On the other hand, iron and copper react easily with moist air and get corroded (iron rusts and copper develops a green coating), so they are not suitable for jewellery.

questions.text: Write the functions of xylem and phloem tissue (one for each).

parts.statement: Write the functions of xylem and phloem tissue (one for each).
parts.explanation:
Answer:
1. Function of Xylem: It transports water and dissolved minerals absorbed by the roots upward to the leaves and other parts of the plant.
2. Function of Phloem: It transports food prepared in the leaves (during photosynthesis) to all other parts of the plant. (Memory trick: 'Ph'loem = 'F'ood).

questions.text: Define reflex action. Write two examples of reflex actions.

parts.statement: Define reflex action. Write two examples of reflex actions.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Definition: A sudden, quick, and automatic (involuntary) response to an external stimulus without conscious thinking is called a 'reflex action'. It is mainly controlled by the spinal cord.

Two Examples:
1. Immediately pulling your hand away upon accidentally touching a hot object.
2. Blinking of eyes or narrowing of pupils when bright light suddenly falls on them.

questions.text: What is the effect of iodine deficiency on the function of the thyroid gland? Write the name of the disease caused by it.

parts.statement: What is the effect of iodine deficiency on the function of the thyroid gland? Write the name of the disease caused by it.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Effect: The thyroid gland needs iodine to produce the 'thyroxine hormone'. Due to iodine deficiency, thyroxine production decreases, which disturbs the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats in the body, causing the thyroid gland to swell.

Disease Caused: Goitre (characterized by a swollen neck).

questions.text: Define pollination. How many types of pollination are there?

parts.statement: Define pollination. How many types of pollination are there?
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Definition: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther (male part) of a flower to the stigma (female part) of the same flower or another flower is called 'pollination'.

Types of Pollination: It is of two types –
1. Self-pollination
2. Cross-pollination

questions.text: Define dominant traits and recessive traits.

parts.statement: Define dominant traits and recessive traits.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
1. Dominant Trait: When two plants with contrasting characters are crossed, the trait that expresses itself clearly in the first generation (F₁) is called a dominant trait (e.g., tallness 'T' in pea plants).
2. Recessive Trait: The trait that remains hidden and does not express itself in the first generation (F₁) is called a recessive trait (e.g., dwarfness 't' in pea plants).

questions.text: An electric heater of resistance 8 Ω draws a current of 15 Amp from the mains for 2 hours. Calculate the rate at which heat is produced in the heater.

parts.statement: An electric heater of resistance 8 Ω draws a current of 15 Amp from the mains for 2 hours. Calculate the rate at which heat is produced in the heater.
parts.explanation:
Answer:

Given:
Resistance (R) = 8 Ω (Note: '82' in the printed paper is a typo for 8 Ω as per the standard NCERT question)
Current (I) = 15 A
Time (t) = 2 hours

Note: 'Rate at which heat is produced' simply means Electric Power (P).

Formula:
Rate of heat produced (P) = I² × R

Calculation:
P = (15)² × 8
P = 225 × 8
P = 1800 Watt (or 1800 J/s)

Answer: The rate at which heat is produced in the heater is 1800 Watts (1800 J/s).

questions.text: Why is a fuse used in an electric circuit? Explain.

parts.statement: Why is a fuse used in an electric circuit? Explain.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
A fuse wire is used in an electric circuit as a safety device to protect household appliances (like TVs, fridges, and fans) from damage. If an excessively high current flows due to a short circuit or overloading, the low-melting-point fuse wire heats up, melts immediately, and breaks the circuit to stop the current.

questions.text: What is an ecosystem? Write the names of its two major components.

parts.statement: What is an ecosystem? Write the names of its two major components.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Definition: A natural self-sustaining system formed by the interaction of all living organisms (plants, animals, microbes) with the non-living physical environment (air, water, soil, sunlight) of an area is called an 'ecosystem' (e.g., a pond or forest).

Two Major Components:
1. Biotic components (all living things – producers, consumers, decomposers)
2. Abiotic components (non-living factors – temperature, rainfall, air, soil)

questions.text:
Draw the electron-dot structure of the following:
(i) H₂   (ii) O₂   (iii) N₂

parts.statement:
Draw the electron-dot structure of the following:
(i) H₂   (ii) O₂   (iii) N₂
parts.explanation:
Answer:
In covalent bonding, atoms share their outermost (valence) electrons to complete their octet (or duplet in hydrogen):

(i) Hydrogen molecule (H₂):
Each H atom has 1 valence electron. Both share 1 electron each to form a single bond (H–H).
Structure:  H : H

(ii) Oxygen molecule (O₂):
Each O atom has 6 valence electrons. To complete their octet, both share 2 electrons each to form a double bond (O=O).
Structure:  :Ö :: Ö:

(iii) Nitrogen molecule (N₂):
Each N atom has 5 valence electrons. To complete their octet, both share 3 electrons each to form a triple bond (N≡N).
Structure:  :N ⋮⋮ N:

parts.statement:
Draw the electron-dot structure of the following:
(i) CH₄   (ii) C₂H₆   (iii) CO₂
parts.explanation:
Answer:

(i) Methane (CH₄):
Carbon has 4 valence electrons. It shares 1 electron each with 4 hydrogen atoms to form four single covalent bonds.
          H
          :
      H : C : H
          :
          H

(ii) Ethane (C₂H₆):
Two carbon atoms share 1 electron pair with each other, and their remaining 3 valence electrons form single bonds with 6 hydrogen atoms.
        H   H
        :   :
    H : C : C : H
        :   :
        H   H

(iii) Carbon dioxide (CO₂):
The central carbon atom shares 2 electrons each with two oxygen atoms on either side, forming two double bonds (O=C=O).
Structure:  :Ö :: C :: Ö:

questions.text: Draw a labelled diagram of the female reproductive system.

parts.statement: Draw a labelled diagram of the female reproductive system.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Draw a neat pencil diagram of the human female reproductive system in your answer sheet and clearly label these main parts:

1. Ovary: A pair of ovaries that produce eggs (ova) and female hormones.
2. Oviduct (Fallopian tube): The tube where fertilization of the egg by sperm takes place.
3. Uterus (Womb): The elastic bag-like structure where the embryo grows and develops.
4. Cervix: The lower narrow neck of the uterus.
5. Vagina: The muscular passage opening outside from the cervix.

parts.statement: If an interesting activity needs to be designed to understand the difference between sexual and asexual reproduction, what kind of activity can be prepared?
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Activity Name: 'Garden & Seed Observation' (Hands-on Comparison Activity)

Materials Required: A potato with buds ('eyes'), a rose stem cutting, a few pea or gram seeds, two pots, and soil.

Procedure:
1. In Pot (A), plant the potato piece and rose stem cutting. After a few days, new plants grow from them. Here, only a single parent plant part was used—this is 'asexual reproduction', and all new plants look identical (clones) to the parent.
2. In Pot (B), sow the pea seeds. These seeds were formed by the fusion of male and female gametes in a flower—this is 'sexual reproduction'. The new plants grown from seeds show slight variations in height, leaf size, or flower colour.

Conclusion: Through this simple activity, students can easily observe that asexual reproduction involves one parent and produces identical offspring, whereas sexual reproduction involves two parents and creates variations.

questions.text: What is myopia (nearsightedness)? Write its cause and ways to correct it.

parts.statement: What is myopia (nearsightedness)? Write its cause and ways to correct it.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Definition: Myopia (nearsightedness) is a vision defect in which a person can see nearby objects clearly, but distant objects appear blurry. In this defect, the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina instead of on the retina.

Causes:
1. Excessive curvature of the eye lens (decrease in focal length).
2. Elongation of the eyeball.

Correction:
This defect is corrected by wearing spectacles with a 'concave lens' of suitable power, which diverges incoming light rays so that the image forms accurately on the retina.

parts.statement: What is hypermetropia? Write its cause and ways to correct it.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Definition: Hypermetropia (farsightedness) is a vision defect in which a person can see distant objects clearly, but nearby objects (like reading a book) appear blurry. In this defect, the image of a nearby object is formed behind the retina.

Causes:
1. Focal length of the eye lens becomes too long.
2. The eyeball becomes too small.

Correction:
This defect is corrected by using spectacles with a 'convex lens' of suitable power, which converges light rays so that the image focuses properly on the retina.

questions.text:
Write balanced chemical equations for the following chemical reactions:
(i) Hydrogen + Chlorine ⟶ Hydrogen Chloride
(ii) Barium Chloride + Aluminium Sulphate ⟶ Barium Sulphate + Aluminium Chloride
(iii) Sodium + Water ⟶ Sodium Hydroxide + Hydrogen
(iv) Zinc Carbonate ⟶ Zinc Oxide + Carbon Dioxide

parts.statement:
Write balanced chemical equations for the following chemical reactions:
(i) Hydrogen + Chlorine ⟶ Hydrogen Chloride
(ii) Barium Chloride + Aluminium Sulphate ⟶ Barium Sulphate + Aluminium Chloride
(iii) Sodium + Water ⟶ Sodium Hydroxide + Hydrogen
(iv) Zinc Carbonate ⟶ Zinc Oxide + Carbon Dioxide
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Balancing the number of atoms on both sides of the arrow gives the following equations:

(i) Hydrogen + Chlorine ⟶ Hydrogen Chloride
Equation: H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) ⟶ 2HCl(g)

(ii) Barium Chloride + Aluminium Sulphate ⟶ Barium Sulphate + Aluminium Chloride
Equation: 3BaCl₂(aq) + Al₂(SO₄)₃(aq) ⟶ 3BaSO₄(s) + 2AlCl₃(aq)

(iii) Sodium + Water ⟶ Sodium Hydroxide + Hydrogen
Equation: 2Na(s) + 2H₂O(l) ⟶ 2NaOH(aq) + H₂(g)

(iv) Zinc Carbonate ⟶ Zinc Oxide + Carbon Dioxide
Equation: ZnCO₃(s) ⟶ ZnO(s) + CO₂(g)

parts.statement:
Write balanced chemical equations for the following chemical reactions:
(i) Calcium Hydroxide + Carbon Dioxide ⟶ Calcium Carbonate + Water
(ii) Zinc + Silver Nitrate ⟶ Zinc Nitrate + Silver
(iii) Aluminium + Copper Chloride ⟶ Aluminium Chloride + Copper
(iv) Barium Chloride + Potassium Sulphate ⟶ Barium Sulphate + Potassium Chloride
parts.explanation:
Answer:
The balanced chemical equations are as follows:

(i) Calcium Hydroxide + Carbon Dioxide ⟶ Calcium Carbonate + Water
Equation: Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂(g) ⟶ CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l)

(ii) Zinc + Silver Nitrate ⟶ Zinc Nitrate + Silver
Equation: Zn(s) + 2AgNO₃(aq) ⟶ Zn(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2Ag(s)

(iii) Aluminium + Copper Chloride ⟶ Aluminium Chloride + Copper
Equation: 2Al(s) + 3CuCl₂(aq) ⟶ 2AlCl₃(aq) + 3Cu(s)

(iv) Barium Chloride + Potassium Sulphate ⟶ Barium Sulphate + Potassium Chloride
Equation: BaCl₂(aq) + K₂SO₄(aq) ⟶ BaSO₄(s) + 2KCl(aq)

questions.text: Write any four differences between Aerobic and Anaerobic respiration.

parts.statement: Write any four differences between Aerobic and Anaerobic respiration.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Four major differences between Aerobic and Anaerobic respiration are given below:

| S.No. | Basis | Aerobic Respiration | Anaerobic Respiration |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Presence of Oxygen | It takes place in the presence of oxygen (O₂). | It takes place in the absence of oxygen (O₂). |
| 2. | Breakdown of Glucose | Complete breakdown (oxidation) of glucose occurs. | Incomplete breakdown of glucose occurs. |
| 3. | End Products | Carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O) are formed. | Ethanol (in yeast) or lactic acid (in muscles) is formed. |
| 4. | Amount of Energy | A large amount of energy (38 ATP) is released. | Very little energy (only 2 ATP) is released. |
| 5. | Site of Reaction | It occurs in both cytoplasm and mitochondria. | It occurs only in the cytoplasm. |

parts.statement: Write any four differences between arteries and veins.
parts.explanation:
Answer:
Four major differences between arteries and veins are given below:

| S.No. | Basis | Artery | Vein |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Direction of Blood Flow | Carries blood away from the heart to various body organs. | Brings blood back from body organs to the heart. |
| 2. | Type of Blood | Carries oxygenated (pure) blood. (Exception: Pulmonary artery) | Carries deoxygenated (impure) blood. (Exception: Pulmonary vein) |
| 3. | Wall Structure | Walls are thick, elastic, and muscular because blood flows under high pressure. | Walls are thin and less elastic because blood flows under low pressure. |
| 4. | Valves | Valves are absent. | Valves are present to prevent the backward flow of blood. |

questions.text:
Draw ray diagrams to show image formation by a concave mirror and write about the position and nature of the image in each of the following cases:
(i) When the object is placed between C and F
(ii) When the object is placed at F.

parts.statement:
Draw ray diagrams to show image formation by a concave mirror and write about the position and nature of the image in each of the following cases:
(i) When the object is placed between C and F
(ii) When the object is placed at F.
parts.explanation:
Answer:

(i) When the object is placed between Centre of Curvature (C) and Principal Focus (F):
• Ray Diagram: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the focus (F) after reflection, and a ray passing through C reflects back along the same path. Both rays meet beyond C.
• Position of Image: Beyond the centre of curvature (C).
• Nature and Size: Real, inverted, and enlarged (magnified).

(ii) When the object is placed at the Principal Focus (F):
• Ray Diagram: Reflected rays from an object placed at F travel parallel to each other and meet at infinity.
• Position of Image: At infinity.
• Nature and Size: Real, inverted, and highly enlarged.

parts.statement:
Draw ray diagrams to show image formation by a convex lens and describe the position and nature of the image in each of the following cases:
(i) When the object is placed between F₁ and 2F₁
(ii) When the object is placed at 2F₁.
parts.explanation:
Answer:

(i) When the object is placed between F₁ and 2F₁:
• Ray Diagram: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through focus (F₂) on the other side after refraction, and a ray passing through the optical centre (O) goes straight without deviation. Both rays intersect beyond 2F₂.
• Position of Image: Beyond 2F₂ on the other side of the lens.
• Nature and Size: Real, inverted, and enlarged (magnified).

(ii) When the object is placed at 2F₁:
• Ray Diagram: Both refracted rays from an object placed at 2F₁ intersect right at 2F₂ on the opposite side of the lens.
• Position of Image: At 2F₂ on the other side of the lens.
• Nature and Size: Real, inverted, and of the exact same size as the object.
